## Technical analysis (June 27 UTC — confirmed final close 01:15 UTC June 28)

**Crypto.com MCP confirmed final close data:** Open $60,104.10 / High $60,947.94 / Low $59,855.73 / Close $60,024.33. Full-session volume: 1,466.02 BTC ($88.0M). Change −$78.77 (−0.13%) from June 26 close. CORRECTION from morning partial read (20:05 UTC) which showed $60,241.43 — the confirmed close is $217 lower.

**Day 5 exit gate CONFIRMED.** Five consecutive UTC closes below $63,500: June 23 ($62,724.97) → June 24 ($61,078.01) → June 25 ($59,795.45) → June 26 ($60,103.10) → June 27 ($60,024.33). The distribution phase is now five sessions deep with a confirmed lower close on June 27 vs June 26.

**Shooting star candle — confirmed more bearish.** The June 27 session printed a confirmed shooting star: open $60,104 → high $60,948 → close $60,024. The intraday reversal spread (high to close) is $923.61 — more bearish than the morning's $707 estimate based on partial data. BTC closed $79 below the prior session close, confirming the rejection at $61,000 was not just intraday but structural: sellers stepped in above $60,948 and drove price below the prior session's close level. This is the most bearish candle in the five-session sequence by close-vs-prior-close metric.

**Key fact:** The $60,024.33 close is only $24.33 above the psychologically critical $60,000 round number. A June 29 open with any negative catalyst (weak Asia, NVDA stop trigger) could breach $60,000 in thin Sunday/early Monday trading.

**Trend read:** BTC is in a confirmed intermediate downtrend (5 consecutive exit-gate closes). Price is trading below all key moving averages. The declining session closes: June 23 ($62,725) → June 24 ($61,078) → June 25 ($59,795) → June 26 ($60,103) → June 27 ($60,024) show clear staircase distribution. The June 26 mini-bounce (+$307) was negated by June 27's close (-$79 below June 26).

**Strongest resistance:** $62,000 (★ re-entry gate). Confirmed by: (1) the formal re-entry framework gate; (2) the June 25 session high $61,967 (failed at this level); (3) the June 27 shooting star rejected at $60,948 — well below $62,000, meaning sellers step in at $61,000 before price can even challenge the re-entry gate; (4) the entire June 23–27 distribution phase has been unable to sustain above $61,000.

**Critical support level:** $60,000 (★ round number). The June 27 close of $60,024.33 is only $24.33 above $60,000. A sustained close below $60,000 would be a new psychological threshold breach and likely attract additional put buying. Below $60,000, next structural supports are $59,855 (June 27 low), $58,325 (June 26 low), $58,100 (June 25 low).

**Volume analysis:** 1,466.02 BTC ($88.0M) full session — above the morning estimate of 1,352.64 BTC but still approximately 75% below a typical weekday. Volume did not spike on the high of $60,948 — confirming thin-market dynamics. However, the additional selling in hours 20–24 UTC (which drove the close from $60,241 partial to $60,024 confirmed) came without a significant volume spike, suggesting sustained algorithmic distribution rather than forced institutional selling.

**Higher-low basing signal (intraday lows):** Three consecutive higher lows confirmed: $58,100 (June 25) → $58,325 (June 26) → $59,856 (June 27). This is constructive on the intraday low side. However, the closing sequence is NOT confirming the same signal — June 25 close $59,795 → June 26 close $60,103 → June 27 close $60,024 shows the close-side recovery attempt was reversed. Two separate signals: intraday lows suggest capitulation slowing; confirmed closes suggest distribution is still ongoing.

**What would invalidate the bear read:** A June 29 UTC close above $62,000 combined with IBIT net daily inflows > $100M would activate Day 1 of the re-entry clock. A confirmed June 29 close above $63,500 would exit the exit-gate sequence and would require a full re-assessment of the distribution thesis. These require +3.3% and +5.8% from the confirmed close of $60,024.33, respectively.
